votes.evidence: Premise confirmed by tracing callers. The only initial-review path is: TaskRun post_save receiver `handle_task_run_saved` (products/review_hog/backend/receivers.py:126-139) -> `transaction.on_commit(_start_stamphog_review)` -> `queue_inbox_pr_review` (products/stamphog/backend/facade/api.py:149-155), which does a bare `process_inbox_pr_review.delay(...)` with no durable record. `_start_stamphog_review` wraps that in `try/except Exception: logger.exception(...)` (receivers.py:224-234), so a publish failure is logged and dropped. The queued task's own comment admits the gap: "the toggle-gated initial review has no webhook redelivery behind it" (products/stamphog/backend/tasks/tasks.py:1158-1160); its `max_retries=3` retries (tasks.py:1109, 1151-1163, 1233) only run after the broker accepted the task. The webhook carve-out cannot recover it: `_HEAD_CHANGING_ACTIONS = {"synchronize","reopened"}` (tasks.py:49) and `_inbox_rereview_carve_out` returns empty for any other action (tasks.py:165-166), while `_review_skip_reason` refuses the bot-authored draft on the normal path (tasks.py:228-233). Repeat TaskRun output saves with `pr_url` do re-fire the receiver (tasks webhook backstop is idempotent and writes once, products/tasks/backend/webhooks.py:277-297; `set_task_run_output` is one save, products/tasks/backend/facade/api.py:2139-2154), but none is guaranteed after the PR-open save, and a `pr_merged` re-fire arrives when the PR is already closed (tasks.py:1166-1169 returns "not_open"). No `task_publish_retry` override exists in posthog/celery.py or posthog/settings/celery.py, so only Celery's default sub-second publish retry policy applies.
votes.refutation: Attempted refutations: (1) The design deliberately treats both legs as fire-and-forget: `_start_stamphog_review` docstring says "the broker being down must never surface into the saver" and test `test_stamphog_queue_failure_never_raises_into_the_save_path` (products/review_hog/backend/tests/test_inbox_trigger.py:358-368) pins "cost a log line" as the contract, "same as the ReviewHog leg" (whose Temporal start is equally non-durable, receivers.py:238-260). So this is a known, accepted trade-off, not an oversight, and it is the same exposure every plain `.delay()` in the codebase has. (2) Celery's default `task_publish_retry=True` absorbs sub-second broker blips. (3) Any later push to the self-driving PR self-heals via the webhook carve-out (tasks.py:49, 165-215), and any later TaskRun output save re-fires the receiver (tasks.py:1119-1121 docstring). (4) The trigger requires a broker outage longer than the publish retry window coinciding with the single PR-open save, which is rare. These reduce the blast radius to one missed draft-time verdict during a real broker outage, but do not make the loss impossible, and there is no manual re-trigger for a bot-authored draft on the label path. Hence real but minor; the proposed outbox worker is heavier than the frequency warrants (a periodic sweep for eligible PRs without a ReviewRun, or nothing, is proportionate). Note SB8 is the same defect reported at the receiver side.

votes.refutation: Attempted refutations: (1) later pushes recover it - true only partially: a `synchronize`/`reopened` delivery creates a fresh run via the webhook carve-out (tasks.py:167-215), so a review does eventually happen if the agent pushes again, but the draft-time verdict the leg exists for (tasks.py:1114-1115) is still missing and a PR with no further push is never reviewed. (2) Celery retries the publish - only 3 retries within ~1s by default, so a broker outage longer than that still drops it. (3) Repeat TaskRun output saves re-fire the receiver - not guaranteed (see evidence); the validator already conceded this. (4) Precedent: the sibling ReviewHog leg `_start_review` (receivers.py:237+, test at test_inbox_trigger.py:302 "temporal down") has the identical fire-and-forget contract and was accepted, so this PR mirrors an existing design choice rather than regressing one. Net: the defect is real but narrow - it needs Redis (CELERY_BROKER_URL = REDIS_URL, posthog/settings/celery.py:26) to be unreachable for more than ~1s at the exact moment of the PR-open save, which would be a wide incident anyway, and a new push works around it. The outbox suggestion is disproportionate; the cheap fix (a scheduled sweep for eligible PRs without a ReviewRun, or retrying the publish with a longer policy) is a nice-to-have. The finding's should_fix priority is too high; downgrade to consider. Note the PR (#75215) is CLOSED, an experiment branch.

votes.evidence: Mechanism confirmed in the worktree. `queue_inbox_pr_review` (products/stamphog/backend/facade/api.py:127-155) writes no durable state; its only action is `process_inbox_pr_review.delay(...)` at api.py:149-155. The caller `_start_stamphog_review` (products/review_hog/backend/receivers.py:213-235) wraps that call in `try/except Exception` and only calls `logger.exception("review_hog_stamphog_inbox_review_queue_failed")` at receivers.py:234-235. The dispatch is registered via `transaction.on_commit` at receivers.py:130-138, and the production writer `set_task_run_output` saves in autocommit (products/tasks/backend/facade/api.py:2149) so the callback runs immediately with nothing stored on failure. Celery publish retry is the library default (no `CELERY_TASK_PUBLISH_RETRY*` override anywhere under posthog/, ee/ or products/; posthog/celery.py:84 loads settings with the CELERY_ namespace and posthog/settings/celery.py:26 sets only `CELERY_BROKER_URL = REDIS_URL`), so only sub-second blips (3 retries at ~0.2s) are absorbed; a Redis outage of a few seconds loses the publish. The retries inside `process_inbox_pr_review` (products/stamphog/backend/tasks/tasks.py:1109, 1137-1160, 1225-1227) all run after the broker accepted the task. Reachability: the trigger is a Redis broker outage at the moment the sandbox agent records `pr_url`; that is a real production event, not a test-only configuration. Recovery is partial, not absent: the stamphog webhook carve-out only re-reviews on `synchronize`/`reopened`/base retarget (tasks.py:49 `_HEAD_CHANGING_ACTIONS = frozenset({"synchronize", "reopened"})`, gate at tasks.py:167), and the `opened` delivery is refused as `bot_author` by `_review_skip_reason` (tasks.py:230-233), so a PR that never gets another push stays without an initial Stamphog verdict. Later TaskRun output saves re-fire the receiver (receivers.py:76-80 docstring; tasks.py:1125-1127), but the only guaranteed later output write is `pr_merged` (products/tasks/backend/webhooks.py:229-235), and by then `process_inbox_pr_review` returns at `state != "open"` (tasks.py:1166-1169); `_record_run_pr_url` (webhooks.py:203-213) is a no-op once pr_url already exists.
votes.refutation: Attempted refutations: (1) Celery publish retry - present by default but only ~0.6s total, does not cover an outage. (2) Webhook redelivery - the `opened` event is bot-author-refused and the carve-out is explicitly scoped to later head-changing deliveries (tasks.py:160-165 docstring), so it only recovers when the bot pushes again. (3) Receiver re-fire on later saves - exists but no post-`pr_url` open-state output save is guaranteed. (4) Design intent - this is a deliberate, tested trade-off: `test_stamphog_queue_failure_never_raises_into_the_save_path` (products/review_hog/backend/tests/test_inbox_trigger.py:358-368) states "the Celery broker being down must cost a log line", mirroring the ReviewHog Temporal leg `_start_review` (receivers.py:246, 279-280) which has the identical fire-and-forget loss. None of these make the loss impossible, so the finding survives. Severity is reduced to consider rather than should_fix: the word "permanently" overstates it (any later push re-reviews via the webhook carve-out), the blast radius is one missing draft-time Stamphog verdict per inbox PR during a broker outage, a Redis outage loses every other Celery dispatch in PostHog the same way, and the same gap was consciously accepted for the sibling ReviewHog leg. An outbox is disproportionate to the observed frequency; a cheap reconciliation sweep would be the fitting fix if this is ever seen in practice.
